plan.txt.text:
Reference is qualified c942b254 production (current branch 81239c3e); source d4b5eb56bf24654e510231f1d1251f592cefa185519376dff47190ac3d20649c, WASM 6a47ef4a9a66b15245bc18bb4ee6c3a457434ab80d9cd42effc62506319e32b3. Target remains full default compilation <7000 ns per charged frame, exact output/work, quality unchanged.

Hypothesis: cached ordered neighborhood queries often contain contiguous groups of similarly oriented lines. Store normal component extrema for each fixed block of eight query entries. Monotonic rounded multiply/add with the current finite velocity bounds every original direction dot product. If the minimum is strictly positive, copy the whole ordered block; if the maximum is nonpositive, skip it; otherwise run the original per-line predicate and compaction. No arithmetic used by the physics response changes. Degenerate/nonfinite normals or unbounded intermediate dots take the ordinary path. No reordering or deduplication. Cached metadata invalidates with the existing owning query and grid epoch.

First run an untimed shadow diagnostic, counting blocks/lines classified uniformly while asserting every actual predicate agrees. Then native tests and independent replay. If promising, one fixed 12-pair default compile screen versus the reference, require KEEP; no tuning block sizes from timings or extending an unsuccessful screen. Fresh 24-pair confirmation of the frozen candidate, required full structural gates, broad/large regression guards, fresh WASM memory and isolated stepping before retention. Same runtime/build flags, runner, warmup, fixture, denominator and CPU2 affinity. Timing runs alone.

Monotonicity argument: for a finite velocity component, choose the minimum and maximum normal component endpoints in its sign order. Rounded multiplication is monotone, as is rounded addition. Evaluating the identical two-product-plus-add expression at those endpoints therefore encloses each original rounded dot. Only use finite ordered endpoints and finite resulting lower/upper dots; otherwise the block falls back to exact predicates. Signed zero can change only a zero sign, never the strict >0 decision. Nonfinite normals invalidate a block certificate.
